However, the Rams, with two Ls, might be slightly more desperate than Philadelphia. And then over in the AFC, we've got Patrick Mahomes playing like he's back to his old form and Kirk Cousins lighting up the scoreboard. Let's dive into how I'm wagering on the weekend. Rams @ Eagles Simply put, I don’t think the Eagles are very good right now, and it might not be their year. I did not like the hiring of a first-time offensive coordinator to pair with Jalen Hurts and the results so far are on par with what I expected — a disjointed offense that ranks 17th in offensive DVOA. Hurts is ranked 27th in EPA per play. The Eagles' offensive line hasn’t been its usual self and I think the play-calling hasn’t made much sense. The Rams' defense is fourth in DVOA this season and should be able to disrupt the Eagles' offense in a meaningful way this Sunday. On the other side is an L.A. offense that has shown brilliant moments this season, while also displaying some weaknesses. Last week against the Broncos, the Rams started fast on offense and then disappeared, punctuated by a Matthew Stafford pick-six. Matthew Stafford will try to lead the Rams over the Eagles in NFL Week 4. (Getty Images) The possible return of Puka Nacua will help the Rams' passing attack. On paper, the Rams' offensive line should struggle in this game, but the Eagles' defensive line has been underwhelming. PFF has the Eagles' pass rush ranked 27th in the NFL and the tackling is ranked at about that level, too. The Rams are 1-2, and after blowing that game on Sunday, they need to win this weekend. You shouldn’t just solely wager on teams because they need to win, but that’s part of the equation for me. I get a better quarterback and a better coach who’s playing better football. Schwartz's Pick: Rams -3 Chiefs @ Raiders The Chiefs are 3-0 and playing better football on offense than they have in years. Mahomes looks completely healthy after missing the end of the season with an ACL injury. It was assumed Mahomes would be less mobile, but he’s been moving around the pocket and down the field like usual. In the Chiefs' first game against an excellent Broncos defense, he rushed for 23 yards. In Week 2 against the Colts, he rushed for 17 yards in an overtime win. Patrick Mahomes seems to have found his groove again. (Getty Images) Last week, Mahomes only rush attempt was when he kneeled. The Chiefs' offensive line has played fine this season, but the pass protection has been a concern. Now this group has to play Maxx Crosby and that’s a recipe for pressure on Mahomes. When Mahomes feels pressure or understands it might be a game featuring pressure, he tends to run the ball more often. Kansas City might also need to keep up with the Raiders' scoring output if Cousins continues to put up points for the Raiders. That will lead to a more aggressive Mahomes rushing the football. The Lions’ “Sonic and Knuckles” duo in the backfield was one of the best in the league over the past few years. However, Montgomery was always second fiddle to Jahmyr Gibbs in Detroit. He was always productive, especially in the red zone, but now he has the chance to be the RB1 for the Texans. Over the past three seasons, Montgomery has scored 33 touchdowns on the ground, despite being in that backup role. Now, he should get almost all of the touches when Houston is in the scoring area. The Bills had an awful run defense last season. They ranked 31st in the NFL in defensive EPA/rush and 25th in defensive rushing success rate. This Houston team has struggled with pass protection over the past couple of seasons, so it should try to take advantage of that poor run defense and get the ball to Montgomery whenever possible. David Montgomery should start his Houston tenure with a touchdown. Garrett Wilson 6+ Receptions (-121) During the offseason, new Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich described Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall as the Jets’ “bell cows.” The Jets aren’t a great team, but they know they have two very reliable and dangerous weapons in Wilson and Hall. To make things easy on Geno Smith, Reich will want to scheme ways to get the ball to those two players as often as possible. Wilson dealt with an injury that kept him out for most of last season, but in the first six games of the season when he was fit, Wilson had at least six catches in four of those six games. Geno Smith did not have a good season in Las Vegas, but he had a terrible offensive line and a bad group of skill position players. He might not get back to the guy he was in Seattle, but he should have a much better season with an underrated Jets offensive line protecting him. Smith might have turnover issues, but he is not afraid to let it fly. Since the start of the 2022 season, he ranks fourth in the NFL in pass attempts. This Titans defense is very vulnerable, and Frank Reich should let Geno Smith chuck it early and often in this game. Last season, the Titans ranked 29th in the NFL in defensive EPA/pass and 26th in dropback success rate. This is a good early matchup for Smith to get his feet under him in a Jets uniform (for the second time) and feed his WR1 Garrett Wilson. Omarion Hampton Over 68.5 Rushing Yards (-114) This should be a big season for Omarion Hampton. He only played nine games in his rookie season for the Chargers, but he is set for a huge role in what should be a productive Los Angeles offense. This is a good matchup for him to start the season against the Cardinals. Last season, Arizona ranked 22nd in the NFL in defensive EPA/rush and 23rd in defensive rushing success rate. That defense has a lot of young, inexperienced pieces and should struggle again this season. The Chargers should feed the ball to Hampton early and often to control the game against Arizona. The Chargers are also big favorites and should lead this game down the stretch. That should lead to a lot of carries for Hampton down the stretch while the Chargers put the game on ice. articles.text: Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions Skip to content Purchase Watch & Listen Login Dashboard Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions By Josh Shepardson | 2026-09-13T09:01:27-04:00 Sep 13, 2026 | View Larger Image NFL Best Prop Bets: Week 1 Picks Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) Sharp Betting Tools: NFL Props: Lines & Odds NFL Spreads, Totals, & Moneylines NFL Weather Forecast & Potential Impact NFL Implied Team Totals NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Watson tore his ACL on January 5, 2025, in Week 18 of the 2024 season. He made his season debut last year on October 26, 2025, in Week 8. Remarkably, Watson didn't skip a beat. In fact, he played the best football of his career. The speedster can get off to a fast start this year, and the Packers might lean into the passing attack more while sorting through their backfield with Josh Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List. The matchup against the Vikings could also prompt them to pass more. Per TruMedia, the Vikings were tied for 12th in expected points added (EPA) allowed per designed rush in 2025 and fifth in yards before contact allowed per rush attempt (1.05). Minnesota's coverage tendencies also boost Watson's receiving outlook. According to the Fantasy Points Data Suite 2.0, the Vikings were first in two-high coverage rate (69.0%) and first in blitz rate (44.7%) in 2025. Watson rattled off a 20% target rate per route and 2.42 yards per route run (Y/RR) on 119 routes against two-high coverage in 2025. Furthermore, he had a 26% target rate per route and 2.47 Y/RR on 77 routes against the blitz last season, reeling in 10 receptions on 20 targets for 190 receiving yards. Watson exceeded 55.5 receiving yards only five times in 11 games in 2025. That said, the Packers have thinned their wide receiving corps, and Watson should exceed last year's 68.6% route participation rate in a less crowded wideout room. On a more expansive route participation rate, with a possible uptick in the Packers' passing rate from last year's 24th ranking in pass rate over expected (-2.1% PROE) out of the gate, Watson should clear 55.5 receiving yards. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Kellen Moore brought his fast-paced brand of offense to the Saints last year. New Orleans played at the NFL's fastest pace in 2025, which is favorable for play volume. The Saints were only 19th in PROE (-0.6%), but their passing tendencies ratcheted up down the stretch. In the final four weeks of the regular season, New Orleans was tied for third in PROE (5.0%). They did play the Titans during those four weeks, and Tennessee's defense faced an NFL-high 6.4% PROE. However, the Saints also played the Panthers, Jets, and Falcons in that period, and they ranked 25th (-1.6%), 21st (-0.3%), and 20th (0.3%), respectively, in PROE faced in the 2025 regular season. The Saints had a banged-up backfield at that point, but Moore's willingness to cut Tyler Shough loose can also be viewed as bullish for his trust in the young quarterback. Speaking of Shough, Johnson excelled with the rookie quarterback. In 10 games that Shough played at least 20 snaps last season, Johnson recorded a 71.3% route participation rate, 16.2% target share, 20% target rate per route, 17.7% air yards share, 8.9-yard average depth of target (aDOT), 4.6 receptions per game, 57.4 receiving yards per game, and 1.97 Y/RR. The pass-catching tight end cleared 41.5 receiving yards in five of his last eight games last year. That includes the final three, when he ripped off 89, 95, and 61 receiving yards. Johnson can pick up where he left off for the Saints, and with New Orleans serving as one of the week's biggest underdogs, he should be in a negative gamescript, necessitating the Saints air it out to keep up with Detroit's high-powered offense. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) I'm not on an island on the Sharp Football Analysis team for this pick. Rich Hribar shouted out Brown over 23.5 receiving yards on the NFL Week 1 Best Bets & Player Props Show . A top-down view is immediately favorable for Brown's receiving outlook. Since 2023, the Bengals are tied for first in PROE (7.9%). Conversely, the Buccaneers have been the NFL's biggest pass funnel since 2023, facing the highest PROE (4.3%). The Bengals don't need their arm twisted to let Joe Burrow cook, but the matchup should also push them in that direction. The matchup is also tasty for Brown. In the 2025 regular season, the Bucs allowed the most receiving yards per game (50.1) and the most yards per target (9.90) to running backs. Brown should also be leaned on as an outlet against Todd Bowles ‘ blitz-heavy tendencies. Tampa Bay had the third-highest blitz rate (35.3%) in 2025, and they've had the second-highest blitz rate (40.8%) since 2023. Meanwhile, among players on the Bengals with at least 40 routes against the blitz since 2024, Brown is tied for second in targets per route run (0.25) and has 30 targets, 23 receptions, 158 receiving yards, and 1.30 Y/RR on 122 routes against the blitz. Finally, in 23 games in which Burrow has played at least 20 snaps since 2024, Brown has tallied a 48.0% route participation rate, 11.3% target share, 0.21 TPRR, 3.7 receptions per game, 23.8 receiving yards per game, and 1.20 Y/RR. Brown should surpass those marks against Tampa Bay's pass-funnel and blitz-heavy defense, putting him over 23.5 receiving yards. Commanders @ Cowboys This is a huge NFC East division game and both teams are scrambling for a win after they both dropped their Week 1 tilts. I like the Commanders to keep this game close. Washington lost by two points to the Eagles last weekend and could have won the game. The Eagles only generated 10 first downs but hit multiple explosive plays to score. The Commanders' offense played well (at times) against one of the better defenses in the NFL. Now it faces a Dallas defense that was pathetic on Sunday night against the Giants. The Cowboys' defensive line got dominated by the Giants and the coverage unit got beat multiple times with the same concept. Those are not mistakes that are easily fixed in one week. I think the Commanders' offense should be able to exploit these issues. Daniels will have one week under his belt, after missing most of last season. And we often see big player improvement between Week 1 and Week 2. In this case, I’m banking on it. The Dallas offense was also a dud against the Giants. All that firepower and only three scoring drives. I do think the Cowboys will get it together and play more consistently on offense, but that doesn't mean they will find success. The Washington defense got little attention for its rebuild, but it paid off in Week 1. Yes, Washington lost, but again, it only allowed 10 first downs to Philly. I think the Commanders' D showed it can be good enough to allow the offense to spend more time on the field, and for me, that equals a cover. Schwartz's Pick: Commanders +4.5 Bengals @ Texans There was a lot of chatter after Week 1 that the Bengals' defense was fixed and that's all because they beat the Bucs 33-27. The Bucs scored late to make it a one-score game. It was a Bengals double-digit lead for most of the day. However, if you take a closer look, it’s easy to see that the Bengals' defense did not play as well as reported. The Bucs fumbled the ball four times and the Bengals do get credit for forcing those turnovers. But the Bucs scored on every other drive. They had no punts and 50% on third down. CJ Stroud and the Texans had a solid showing against the Bills in Week 1 (Getty Images). The Texans' offense played well against the Bills on Sunday. It scored 31 points and more importantly, the run game was much improved. Houston spent resources on the offensive line and at running back. It looked much better than it did in 2025. Also, the pass protection looked better. CJ Stroud looked comfortable and more confident. I’d also look for the Texans to be aggressive in this game since they need a win. They cannot start 0-2 against two teams contending for the AFC. So I’d expect them to score points. In a divisional matchup, they’ll be ready, even without Sam Darnold. (11) Chargers | Chargers vs. Raiders I’m not out on the Chargers. They have to put in extra work this week and prepare better. On paper, the Chargers are way better than Las Vegas. (12) Chiefs | Colts vs. Chiefs The Colts’ defense didn’t show up in Week 1. Don’t expect it to be any better against the Chiefs, who now have a wicked running game with Kenneth Walker III. (13) Ravens | Saints vs. Ravens The Saints earned a remarkable comeback against the Lions, but fell a little short. However, it took Tyler Shough an entire half to get cooking. I’m not buying the hype. (14) Eagles | Eagles vs. Titans The Titans are just a below-average squad with coaches that haven’t won in years. (15) Buccaneers | Browns vs. Buccaneers Could this be Deshaun Watson’s final game as a starter for Cleveland? (16) 49ers | 49ers vs. Dolphins Not only is San Francisco better, but the Niners will have much more time to prepare for this game than the Dolphins. That Melbourne win will help, too.
